deduped_items.body_text:
Fidalgo sigue contando para México tras el Mundial; Cucho Hernández se queda fuera de la lista de Colombia
Los dos futbolistas del Betis estuvieron en las convocatorias para el torneo del pasado verano
Tras la disputa de la Copa del Mundo durante el pasado verano, las selecciones nacionales vuelven a la carga. Tras la jornada que este fin de semana medirá al Betis con el Deportivo en La Coruña, los futbolistas citados por sus selecciones participarán en ... los próximos duelos programados durante la pausa del fútbol de clubes. No obstante, dos jugadores del Betis que estuvieron con sus selecciones durante la Copa del Mundo han corrido distinta suerte a la hora de darse a conocer las listas de convocados de sus selecciones.
Son los casos de Álvaro Fidalgo y de Cucho Hernández. El centrocampista ovetense ha sido citado por Rafa Márquez en su primera convocatoria como seleccionador nacional de México, mientras que el delantero no ha sido tenido en cuenta por parte de Néstor Lorenzo, que sí lo quiso tener a sus órdenes durante el torneo del pasado verano.
Álvaro Fidalgo, nacido en España pero con una amplia trayectoria en el fútbol mexicano antes de recalar en el Betis, se estrenó como internacional con el combnado azteca poco antes de que disputara el Mundial en el que México fue una de las anfitrionas. Disputó tres partidos durante la cita en los que consiguió además anotar un gol. Durante este comienzo de temporada apenas ha podido jugar, ya que acumula 60 minutos de juego repartidos en tres encuentros. No obstante, Márquez ha optado por contar con el jugador del Betis en una lista en la que como centrocampistas figuran, además del asturiano, Chávez (Dinamo de Moscú), Vargas (Atlético de Madrid), Cervantes (América), Lira (Cruz Azul), Pineda (Rayados), Mora (Xolos), Márquez (Cruz Azul), Romo (Chivas) y García (Juárez). México se enfrentará a Colombia el 26 de septiembre, el 29 a Perú, el 3 de octubre a Estados Unidos y el 6 a Chile.
Por contra, Cucho Hernández no ha sido citado por Néstor Lorenzo tras el Mundial para los amistosos que medirán al cuadro cafetero con México el 26 de septiembre, con Paraguay el 2 de octubre y con Perú el 6 del mismo mes disputándose todos los partidos en Estados Unidos. En una lista en la que tampoco figura Nelson Deossa, el seleccionador ha optado por los siguientes atacantes: Kevin Viveros (Athlético Paranaense), Carlos Andrés Gómez (Vasco da Gama), Óscar Perea (América), Luis Suárez (Sporting) y Camilo Durán (Celtic).

deduped_items.summary: During the Tweede Divisie amateur football match on Saturday between football clubs IJsselmeervogels and GVVV, after former professional Jhon van Beukering punched Quiermo Dumay, a player for the h
deduped_items.body_text:
Football association suspends ex-pro after punch leaves player with 7 broken teeth
During the Tweede Divisie amateur football match on Saturday between football clubs IJsselmeervogels and GVVV, after former professional Jhon van Beukering punched Quiermo Dumay, a player for the host club IJsselmeervogels, in the face in the locker-room area. Van Beukering has now been provisionally suspended for 60 days by the football association KNVB.

deduped_items.title: Minister's past roles prompt scrutiny of startup funding decisions
deduped_items.summary: Liina Vahtras, who has just become minister of economic affairs and industry, previously served on the management board of the Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS) and also sat on the board of Rochna Invest OÜ — a company whose portfolio startups received a total of €1.25 million in support from EIS during the same period. Prime Minister Kristen Michal said Vahtras acted in accordance with the rules because she did not take part in making the funding decisions.

deduped_items.title: Hungary and Türkiye Explore New Opportunities for Joint Military Training
deduped_items.summary: A professional delegation from the Land Forces of the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command and a delegation from the Turkish General Staff held discussions on opportunities for joint international training exercises. The Hungarian delegation was led by Brigadier General Zsolt Molnár, Deputy Commander for Land Forces at the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command, […] The post Hungary and Türkiye Explore New Opportunities for Joint Military Training appeared first on Hungar
deduped_items.body_text:
The facility is suitable for the maintenance and repair of components such as running gear, auxiliary equipment, and weapon systems.Continue reading
A professional delegation from the Land Forces of the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command and a delegation from the Turkish General Staff held discussions on opportunities for joint international training exercises. The Hungarian delegation was led by Brigadier General Zsolt Molnár, Deputy Commander for Land Forces at the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command, while the Turkish side was represented by Brigadier General Kamil Tumba, Head of Defense Planning and Project Management at the Turkish Land Forces Command.
The visit provided an opportunity for the two nations to build on their existing cooperation and expand knowledge sharing into new areas, primarily in the fields of drone technology, technical support, and chemical defense.
The Turkish delegation learned about the Hungarian Defense Forces’ training system, with particular emphasis on the C-IED training offered by the Hungarian Defense Forces Non-Commissioned Officers’ Academy—that is, training in countering improvised explosive devices.
Another key topic of discussion was the use of these drones.
Based on the Turkish side’s experience, drones are indispensable tools in modern warfare, which is why as many soldiers as possible must learn to use them. The parties also discussed mutual training opportunities in this regard.
The Turkish delegates then visited the Central Firing and Training Range, where they were briefed on the core missions of the Hungarian Defense Forces’ 30th Kinizsi Pál Armored Infantry Brigade by Colonel István Hattyár, the brigade commander. The subsequent static and dynamic demonstrations focused on the Lynx infantry fighting vehicle.
The parties also reviewed equipment from the Turkish defense industry currently in service with the Hungarian Defense Forces (such as the Gidrán) and discussed their operational experiences with these systems. The two-day professional program concluded with a staff-level meeting, during which the two NATO member states identified areas in which they could support each other’s training efforts.
Via honvedelem.hu; Featured photo: honvedelem.hu

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague Unveils Future Metro Stations in Nusle and Náměstí Míru
Prague Morning
Prague’s future Metro Line D has taken another step toward becoming a reality, with new preliminary designs released for two stations planned along the route.
The Prague Public Transit Company (DPP) has presented renderings of the future Náměstí Míru interchange and Nusle station, offering an early look at how the new metro line could change the city’s underground transport network.
The images do not represent the final appearance of either station. DPP plans to select the architectural solutions through a two-stage competition, which will focus on the design of the interiors and the public spaces around the stations.
DPP intends to organise the competition in two stages, using a workshop format. The winning designs are expected to be selected within 18 months of signing the contract with the competition organiser. Preparations for that contract are currently underway.
Náměstí Míru station will connect Metro Lines A and D
The future Náměstí Míru station is planned beneath Sázavská Street, approximately 40 metres underground. It will be built using underground mining methods and will feature a single-vault design with an island platform.
The new station will be located above the existing Line A station, creating a new interchange between the two metro lines.
The design includes two vestibules equipped with escalators and a third access point with an elevator. The renderings show the planned exits towards Vinohradská, Francouzská, and Sázavská streets, as well as an elevator entrance on Korunní Street.
Metroprojekt has also presented a possible design for the outlet of a ventilation shaft in Riegrovy Sady. The structure will form part of the station’s technical infrastructure, although its final appearance may change following the architectural competition.
New Nusle station will serve Náměstí Bratří Synků
The second station featured in the new designs is the future Nusle station, which was previously known as Náměstí Bratří Synků.
The station will be built using cut-and-cover construction methods, with its island platform located approximately 13 metres below ground level. It is planned between Náměstí Bratří Synků and Otakarova Street.
Plans also include an underground parking garage for local residents above the station.
The new renderings show the proposed station entrances on Náměstí Bratří Synků, the northern vestibule beneath Otakarova Street, and the planned completion of the existing urban block.
When will Prague’s Metro Line D open?
Construction of Metro Line D began in 2022 with the section between Pankrác and Ryšánka. Work on the following section, extending towards Nové Dvory, began in June 2026.
The Pankrác–Nové Dvory section is planned to be the first part of the new metro line to open to passengers. DPP currently expects the section to enter service in the second half of 2032.

deduped_items.body_text:
Two New Squares and a Tower Planned Around Holešovice Station
Prague Morning
The area around Prague’s Nádraží Holešovice station is set for a major redevelopment after the international architectural competition for the site was won by Czech studio Chybík + Krištof.
The winning proposal envisions turning the current transport hub and surrounding brownfield into a new urban district, with two public squares, improved connections between public transport services and a new high-rise building designed to become a landmark.
The redevelopment covers roughly eight hectares around the station. Its aim is not only to add new buildings, but also to reorganise one of Prague’s important transport nodes and connect it more closely with the surrounding neighbourhood.
The competition jury selected the proposal by Chybík + Krištof as the winning design.
From transport hub to urban district
Nádraží Holešovice is currently one of Prague’s major transport interchanges, but much of the surrounding area has traditionally been used primarily for transport and other infrastructure.
The redevelopment is intended to change that. Alongside new construction, the project places emphasis on making transfers between different modes of public transport easier and fully accessible.
The project forms part of the wider Nové Holešovice development, which brings together the Prague Public Transit Company and private investors.
CPI Property, EP Real Estate, Penta Real Estate and AKIPIA are among the companies involved. The City of Prague and Prague 7 municipal district are also participating in the project.

deduped_items.body_text:
ČokoFest to Bring Three Days of Chocolate to Galerie Harfa
Prague Morning
Chocolate lovers will have plenty to discover in Prague this October as ČokoFest 2026 returns to Galerie Harfa for three days of tastings, workshops, competitions and sweet treats.
The festival will take place from October 16 to 18, 2026, at the shopping center in Prague 9. Admission is free.
Now in its 14th year, ČokoFest brings together Czech and international producers, including established chocolatiers and smaller makers.
Visitors will be able to sample and buy a wide selection of chocolates and confectionery, including handmade and bean-to-bar products, pralines, cakes, cookies and macarons.
The festival will also feature a range of less conventional chocolate and sweet specialties. Among the offerings will be a chocolate fountain, chocolate kebabs, chocolate-covered fruit, as well as chocolate-infused wine and beer. Other products on sale will include jams, liqueurs, syrups, dried fruits, honey products, coffee and tea.
Exhibitors from several European countries will join Czech producers, giving visitors the opportunity to discover different chocolate styles and specialties while shopping at international sales stalls.
ČokoFest will also feature a program of activities for both adults and children. Visitors can take part in tastings, competitions and creative workshops, while children can enjoy a dedicated zone and entertainment from performers dressed as popular children’s characters.
Cooking demonstrations will be another part of the program, with chefs from local restaurants sharing their experience and showing visitors how to prepare various sweet treats. Some workshops will also focus on chocolate-making techniques that can be tried at home.
The festival is designed as a family-friendly event, with activities taking place throughout the three days. In addition to tasting and shopping, visitors can watch pastry chefs at work, take part in competitions and learn more about the production and preparation of chocolate and other confectionery.
Opening hours:
Friday, October 16: 2:00–6:00 p.m.
Saturday, October 17: 10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m.
Sunday, October 18: 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

Georgian Officials Hope For ‘2.5-Fold’ Growth in Power Generation by 2036
Georgian officials said they hope to increase power generation 2.5 times by 2036 through new investments, presenting a 10-year vision focused on “self-sufficiency,” expanded renewable generation, a greater role in energy transit, and an upgraded transmission grid.
The Georgian Dream officials, including Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze and Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili, revealed their plans as they marked Energy Workers’ Day on September 17, stressing the goals for Georgia to become “fully self-sufficient in electricity by 2036” while linking the Caspian region, the Black Sea, and Europe in “a single energy space.”
According to Kvirishvili, the vision also envisages developing the Black Sea Submarine Cable, which received “Project of Mutual Interest” status from the European Union this year, as well as the broader “Green Corridor” project linking Georgia with Azerbaijan, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania.
‘Ambitious’ 2036 Plan
Speaking at an event taking place near the Zemo Avchala Hydroelectric Power Plant, commonly known as Zahesi, Kobakhidze said that over the past year, the government had “carried out optimization in many directions” and laid the foundation for a “new vision” according to which Georgia’s energy system would develop over the next 10 years.
According to Kobakhidze, the government has a “very ambitious plan,” under which “power generation in Georgia must increase 2.5 times by 2036.”
“This is an ambitious plan, but its implementation is entirely realistic, and of course, our entire team will spare no effort to achieve it,” he said.
Kobakhidze said the government would make maximum efforts to use Georgia’s energy resources and potential “as wisely and rationally as possible,” attract new investment into the energy sector, strengthen infrastructure and support the development of modern technologies.
Kvrivishvili, for her part, said that energy security is a “national goal,” noting that “energy is one of those fields whose smooth operation is often invisible, but even one small disruption in it instantly becomes visible to the entire country.”
She stressed that people remember well, “what it meant to have an energy-weak Georgia,” where “electricity shortages were a standard everyday problem,” arguing that Georgia must no longer become “an energy-vulnerable country” and should instead be “an energy-strong, self-sufficient state of regional importance.”
As Kvrivishvili noted, over the past year, “the strong sides of the energy system, its weaknesses, opportunities, and the challenges that the state must address in advance became more clearly apparent.”
She then highlighted several completed, ongoing, and planned projects in the energy sector.
Kvrivishvili said that three hydropower plants and one wind project had already been constructed in 2026 and by the end of the year, the construction of another hydropower plant, two wind projects and three solar projects would be completed.
“This year, more than 300 megawatts of new renewable capacity will be added to Georgia’s energy system,” she said. “In 2027, with nearly USD 100 million in investment, 12 power plant projects totaling more than 70 megawatts will come into operation.”
Kvrivishvili said that in 2026, with the support of the Asian Development Bank, the government completed the procurement of 250 megawatts of energy storage batteries. Work will begin in 2026 and is expected to be completed by 2029, with Kvrivishvili arguing that it “will ensure the stable and secure functioning of the system, as well as expand the limits for integrating renewable energy.”
The minister also highlighted the authorities’ efforts to revive energy projects that had been stalled for years.

The Georgian Dream officials, including Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze and Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili, revealed their plans as they marked Energy Workers’ Day on September 17, stressing the goals for Georgia to become “fully self-sufficient in electricity by 2036” while linking the Caspian region, the Black Sea, and Europe in “a single energy space.”
According to Kvirishvili, the vision also envisages developing the Black Sea Submarine Cable, which received “Project of Mutual Interest” status from the European Union this year, as well as the broader “Green Corridor” project linking Georgia with Azerbaijan, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania.

According to Kobakhidze, the government has a “very ambitious plan,” under which “power generation in Georgia must increase 2.5 times by 2036.”
“This is an ambitious plan, but its implementation is entirely realistic, and of course, our entire team will spare no effort to achieve it,” he said.
Kobakhidze said the government would make maximum efforts to use Georgia’s energy resources and potential “as wisely and rationally as possible,” attract new investment into the energy sector, strengthen infrastructure and support the development of modern technologies.

As Kvrivishvili noted, over the past year, “the strong sides of the energy system, its weaknesses, opportunities, and the challenges that the state must address in advance became more clearly apparent.”

deduped_items.title: Citizens' initiative demanding restrictions on data centers reaches 50,000 signatures
deduped_items.summary: The petition calls for conditions on how data centres connect to Finland's electricity grid as well as for the introduction of a separate data centre fee.
deduped_items.body_text:
A citizens' initiative calling for tighter legislative control of data centres in Finland has reached the required 50,000 signatures within three days of starting, and it will now proceed to parliament to be debated by MPs.
The petition, entitled 'Datakeskukset kuriin' (roughly translated as 'Rein in the data centres') was launched on Tuesday in the wake of search engine giant Google's announcement last week that it will significantly expand its data centre operations in Finland over the coming years.
The signatories want the government to set conditions on how data centres connect to Finland's electricity grid and operate their business "taking into account the electricity grid's capacity, mandatory backup power, and the utilisation of waste heat".
In addition, the initiative calls for the introduction of a separate data centre fee, which should be calculated based on the "environmental harm caused by operations and the resources used (including electricity, water, land use)".
This would ensure that energy prices remain affordable for households and other industries, the initiative adds.
Finland has become a magnet for data centres in recent years, with companies such as Microsoft and TikTok owner ByteDance recently announcing planned investments.
Finland is an attractive destination for such investment because of the country's climate — which helps reduce the costs associated with the heat produced by data centres — as well as Finland's large supply of low-carbon electricity.

deduped_items.summary: The petition calls for conditions on how data centres connect to Finland's electricity grid as well as for the introduction of a separate data centre fee.
deduped_items.body_text:
A citizens' initiative calling for tighter legislative control of data centres in Finland has reached the required 50,000 signatures within three days of starting, and it will now proceed to parliament to be debated by MPs.
The petition, entitled 'Datakeskukset kuriin' (roughly translated as 'Rein in the data centres') was launched on Tuesday in the wake of search engine giant Google's announcement last week that it will significantly expand its data centre operations in Finland over the coming years.
The signatories want the government to set conditions on how data centres connect to Finland's electricity grid and operate their business "taking into account the electricity grid's capacity, mandatory backup power, and the utilisation of waste heat".
In addition, the initiative calls for the introduction of a separate data centre fee, which should be calculated based on the "environmental harm caused by operations and the resources used (including electricity, water, land use)".
This would ensure that energy prices remain affordable for households and other industries, the initiative adds.
Finland has become a magnet for data centres in recent years, with companies such as Microsoft and TikTok owner ByteDance recently announcing planned investments.
Finland is an attractive destination for such investment because of the country's climate — which helps reduce the costs associated with the heat produced by data centres — as well as Finland's large supply of low-carbon electricity.

deduped_items.title: Sweden Democrat leader sticks to demand for ministerial posts in future government
deduped_items.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has stuck fast to his party's insistence on ministerial posts in any new government and dismissed reports he plans to take a break in his first press conference since the far-right party's unexpected election setback.
deduped_items.body_text:
Asked whether there was any truth to reports in the Swedish media that the far-right party might be willing to drop its demand for its first ministerial posts if that allowed the right-wing parties to win over the Centre Party and so form a government, Åkesson insisted the party's stance was unchanged.
"I have no new position. We are not going to give up any of our demands," he said, arguing that it was up to the Centre Party – which is refusing to support a government that has Left Party ministers or Sweden Democrat influence – to shift its position.
"We have no red lines. We are not the problem; rather, it is other parties that have a bunch of red lines. And a prerequisite for anything to happen is that other parties give up their red lines."
He later argued that as the Sweden Democrats are one of the largest parties in the parliament it was "pretty unreasonable" to expect it to yield, rather than the smaller centrist parties, which he accused of causing "a great deal of parliamentary chaos in Sweden over a very long time".
'Nothing particularly dramatic'
The Sweden Democrats had an unexpectedly poor election result, dropping three percentage points on their result in 2022, but Åkesson played down his party's setback, claiming that he had been surprised throughout the last four years that his party's polling had remained stable even after winning real political power.
"I can say quite honestly that a potential drop in support after four years of taking responsibility and making compromises was part of the calculation when we entered this cooperation four years ago, so we had expected to take a hit from cooperating and compromising with the center-right parties," he said. "It's nothing particularly dramatic; I think all analysts foresaw that this could happen."
He attributed part of the party's drop in support to the so-called 'Churchill Effect', when a politician succeeds so well in their goals that voters no longer see a need to keep them in power and vote for the opposition (just as Britain's wartime leader Winston Churchill lost an election in July 1945 just two months after helping win the Second World War).
"They said we would collapse when we got power. We haven't. On the contrary, the Sweden Democrats remain a large party," he said.
No plans to resign
Åkesson also denied that he had any plans to take a temporary break from leading the party – something that the broadcaster TV4 reported on Thursday, citing anonymous sources within the party.
"And I'm not going to resign," he added quickly before public broadcaster SVT shifted away from his press conference to cover the arrival of Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson at the Swedish parliament to meet Speaker Andreas Norlén, adding later "I'm not going to take a 'pause' either."
He said it was impossible to know who these sources were, but suggested that they were "not particularly well-informed if they even exist".

deduped_items.body_text:
Gadget guide: What students must know before buying
MANILA, Philippines — Before spending their hard-earned savings on a new tool, student buyers need a reliable gadget guide to help them make informed and confident decisions on their next big purchase.
We’ve created a list of things that students should remember, know, and avoid before deciding on their next gadget purchase that will empower their studies in the coming years.
Where do I start planning?
From drafting research papers to delivering group presentations, a student’s daily routine requires a gadget that strikes the balance between performance, storage, build quality, and the right price. But with so many options on the market, knowing where to start your search can feel overwhelming.
The most common pitfall of student buyers is falling into extremes: They pay extra for high-end features that they seldom use, or they settle for cheaper and underpowered alternatives where they sacrifice the workflow needed to get the job done.
To avoid these mistakes, start by listing the specific software your courses or subjects do require. Identifying whether you primarily use productivity ecosystems or cloud suites like Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, or even heavy specialized software, is an essential first step in narrowing down your search for the next gadget purchase.
And here are some points to take care of when beginning to map out in searching for the next gadget:
- Identifying your Primary Use Case — Everyone has a different set of needs, and that’s okay. Remember that computer science and multimedia students require a different set of technical specifications and hardware compared to those in education, humanities, or business courses that typically produce essays and presentations. Thus, it is important to determine what your current technology needs are. You might also want to ask yourself: “How will my next gadget benefit my studies in the long term?”
- Mobility Check — Are you fine prioritizing raw power and screen space with desktops, or do you opt for portability in usage such as tablets, iPads, or laptops?
- Check your current ecosystem — With the current technology that you have, check how it will be compatible with syncing with the new device that you’re planning to buy. In this state, are your existing devices compatible well with the devices you aim for–-like pairing an iPad with a Mac or MacBook? Or pairing an Android tablet with a Windows laptop?
- Set a strict budget for the purchase — Allocate your financial resources wisely for your next device, and stick to what’s readily available to you. Don’t settle for less—and we recommend that if your needs require more powerful software for more powerful gear, then you would want to invest more financially.
RELATED STORY: New parental controls in iOS 27
The big four of gadget spending
When evaluating and canvassing for any gadget purchase, students usually look for these four major factors, ensuring they get the maximum value for their money before deciding on their next purchase:
- Performance
- For Laptops/Desktops: You need to focus on the processor (CPU) and memory (RAM). When using for general schoolwork, you might want to look for at least that is a mid-range processor (e.g., Intel Core i5, AMD Ryzen 5, or the Apple M-Series) that’s paired with at least 16GB of RAM for future-proofing. Enough RAM prevents your system from slowing down when you have multiple browser tabs open, a video call, and document editors open at once.
- For Phones: You may want to opt for a phone with a mid-range to flagship processor. Aim also for at least 8GB of RAM, as well as a 90Hz or 120Hz display refresh rate that gives users reading long documents and scrolling through lecture slides smoothly.
- Storage
- For Laptops/Desktops: Always go for the Solid State Drive (SSD) over a Hard Disk Drive (HDD). Aim to go for 512GB of internal storage when you can.
- For Phones: 128GB of storage is the absolute minimum in the current tech

deduped_items.body_text:
Gadget guide: What students must know before buying
MANILA, Philippines — Before spending their hard-earned savings on a new tool, student buyers need a reliable gadget guide to help them make informed and confident decisions on their next big purchase.
We’ve created a list of things that students should remember, know, and avoid before deciding on their next gadget purchase that will empower their studies in the coming years.
Where do I start planning?
From drafting research papers to delivering group presentations, a student’s daily routine requires a gadget that strikes the balance between performance, storage, build quality, and the right price. But with so many options on the market, knowing where to start your search can feel overwhelming.
The most common pitfall of student buyers is falling into extremes: They pay extra for high-end features that they seldom use, or they settle for cheaper and underpowered alternatives where they sacrifice the workflow needed to get the job done.
To avoid these mistakes, start by listing the specific software your courses or subjects do require. Identifying whether you primarily use productivity ecosystems or cloud suites like Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, or even heavy specialized software, is an essential first step in narrowing down your search for the next gadget purchase.
And here are some points to take care of when beginning to map out in searching for the next gadget:
- Identifying your Primary Use Case — Everyone has a different set of needs, and that’s okay. Remember that computer science and multimedia students require a different set of technical specifications and hardware compared to those in education, humanities, or business courses that typically produce essays and presentations. Thus, it is important to determine what your current technology needs are. You might also want to ask yourself: “How will my next gadget benefit my studies in the long term?”
- Mobility Check — Are you fine prioritizing raw power and screen space with desktops, or do you opt for portability in usage such as tablets, iPads, or laptops?
- Check your current ecosystem — With the current technology that you have, check how it will be compatible with syncing with the new device that you’re planning to buy. In this state, are your existing devices compatible well with the devices you aim for–-like pairing an iPad with a Mac or MacBook? Or pairing an Android tablet with a Windows laptop?
- Set a strict budget for the purchase — Allocate your financial resources wisely for your next device, and stick to what’s readily available to you. Don’t settle for less—and we recommend that if your needs require more powerful software for more powerful gear, then you would want to invest more financially.
RELATED STORY: New parental controls in iOS 27
The big four of gadget spending
When evaluating and canvassing for any gadget purchase, students usually look for these four major factors, ensuring they get the maximum value for their money before deciding on their next purchase:
- Performance
- For Laptops/Desktops: You need to focus on the processor (CPU) and memory (RAM). When using for general schoolwork, you might want to look for at least that is a mid-range processor (e.g., Intel Core i5, AMD Ryzen 5, or the Apple M-Series) that’s paired with at least 16GB of RAM for future-proofing. Enough RAM prevents your system from slowing down when you have multiple browser tabs open, a video call, and document editors open at once.
- For Phones: You may want to opt for a phone with a mid-range to flagship processor. Aim also for at least 8GB of RAM, as well as a 90Hz or 120Hz display refresh rate that gives users reading long documents and scrolling through lecture slides smoothly.
- Storage
- For Laptops/Desktops: Always go for the Solid State Drive (SSD) over a Hard Disk Drive (HDD). Aim to go for 512GB of internal storage when you can.
- For Phones: 128GB of storage is the absolute minimum in the current tech

deduped_items.title: For Aznar Shipping, going public means growth – and dodging third-gen curse
deduped_items.summary: 'My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,' the third-generation Aznar tells Rappler. 'Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest.'
deduped_items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- Kyle Alexander Aznar, the CEO of Aznar Shipping, is determined to break the generational curse that often affects family businesses by preparing to take the company public through an IPO.
- The IPO aims to raise up to P737 million for fleet expansion and is part of Aznar's strategy to ensure the company's success for future generations, emphasizing professional governance and mentorship.
As his family’s shipping legacy prepares to open itself up to the public, Kyle Alexander Aznar had an age-old curse on his mind.
“You know what they say, the third generation is the last generation,” the Aznar Shipping president and CEO told Rappler on Friday, September 18.
He was, of course, referring to the infamous adage that warns family fortunes rarely survives three generations. The first makes the money, second grows it, the third squanders what’s left. Gone, wasted, kaput.
The third-generation Aznar wasn’t about to let that happen. He was only 27 when he suddenly had to take over the family shipping business after his father died. Now 31 and at the helm, he sees one job as more important than simply making money.
“My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,” Aznar told Rappler at the sidelines of his company’s H1 briefing. “We want our business to succeed — not just for my time. It’s really succeeding generations.”
His chosen way to keep the family ship afloat for another generation? Open it up to the public.
Aznar Shipping has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) that could see the Cebu-based company sell as many as one billion primary shares at an indicative price of up to P0.67 each, potentially raising P670 million in gross proceeds for the company. Another 100 million secondary shares could be sold through an overallotment option, bringing the total potential offer size to P737 million.
At this stage, everything still remains subject to book building and approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). Aznar said the company is targeting a December listing, but stressed that he did not want to “jump the gun” on regulators.
A family business trying to grow up
Aznar is hardly the only old name sailing out of Cebu.
Cebu has long been one of the country’s biggest shipping hubs, producing generations of shipping families, from the Gothongs and Robles to the Cokaliongs and the Lims. The Aboitizes were once part of that club too, with Aboitiz Shipping eventually evolving into 2GO, now under the Sy family’s SM group. (READ: As Atlas Mining leaves by 2027, SMIC expects 2GO, renewables to fill gap)
But while many shipping businesses have remained private and closely held, Aznar sees public company governance as part of the antidote to the generational curse.
“Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest. That’s how I first started getting interested in it quite a few years ago,” he told Rappler.
The professionalization actually began before the IPO. Even before the company’s aspirations to go public, the shipping company already had independent directors sitting on its board. Aznar said he has been the only family member on the board for the past three years, surrounded instead by professionals whom he calls his mentors.
“I was just only 27 when I had to take over the company when my dad passed away,” he said. “I was humble enough to realize that I might not have all the answers, I might not always be right.”
That setup, he believes, has paid off.
Aznar Shipping’s revenue jumped from P59.2 million in 2023 to P223.9 million in 2025, when it booked P51.7 million in net income. In just the first six months of 2026, revenue reached P210.9 million while net income hit P53.2 million, already topping the previous full year.
The company currently operates nine vessels across four principal Visayas corridors, with cargo and rolling vehicles accounting for about 86% of first-half revenue.

- The IPO aims to raise up to P737 million for fleet expansion and is part of Aznar's strategy to ensure the company's success for future generations, emphasizing professional governance and mentorship.
As his family’s shipping legacy prepares to open itself up to the public, Kyle Alexander Aznar had an age-old curse on his mind.
“You know what they say, the third generation is the last generation,” the Aznar Shipping president and CEO told Rappler on Friday, September 18.
He was, of course, referring to the infamous adage that warns family fortunes rarely survives three generations. The first makes the money, second grows it, the third squanders what’s left. Gone, wasted, kaput.
The third-generation Aznar wasn’t about to let that happen. He was only 27 when he suddenly had to take over the family shipping business after his father died. Now 31 and at the helm, he sees one job as more important than simply making money.
“My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,” Aznar told Rappler at the sidelines of his company’s H1 briefing. “We want our business to succeed — not just for my time. It’s really succeeding generations.”
His chosen way to keep the family ship afloat for another generation? Open it up to the public.
Aznar Shipping has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) that could see the Cebu-based company sell as many as one billion primary shares at an indicative price of up to P0.67 each, potentially raising P670 million in gross proceeds for the company. Another 100 million secondary shares could be sold through an overallotment option, bringing the total potential offer size to P737 million.
At this stage, everything still remains subject to book building and approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). Aznar said the company is targeting a December listing, but stressed that he did not want to “jump the gun” on regulators.
A family business trying to grow up
Aznar is hardly the only old name sailing out of Cebu.
Cebu has long been one of the country’s biggest shipping hubs, producing generations of shipping families, from the Gothongs and Robles to the Cokaliongs and the Lims. The Aboitizes were once part of that club too, with Aboitiz Shipping eventually evolving into 2GO, now under the Sy family’s SM group. (READ: As Atlas Mining leaves by 2027, SMIC expects 2GO, renewables to fill gap)
But while many shipping businesses have remained private and closely held, Aznar sees public company governance as part of the antidote to the generational curse.
“Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest. That’s how I first started getting interested in it quite a few years ago,” he told Rappler.
The professionalization actually began before the IPO. Even before the company’s aspirations to go public, the shipping company already had independent directors sitting on its board. Aznar said he has been the only family member on the board for the past three years, surrounded instead by professionals whom he calls his mentors.
“I was just only 27 when I had to take over the company when my dad passed away,” he said. “I was humble enough to realize that I might not have all the answers, I might not always be right.”
That setup, he believes, has paid off.
Aznar Shipping’s revenue jumped from P59.2 million in 2023 to P223.9 million in 2025, when it booked P51.7 million in net income. In just the first six months of 2026, revenue reached P210.9 million while net income hit P53.2 million, already topping the previous full year.
The company currently operates nine vessels across four principal Visayas corridors, with cargo and rolling vehicles accounting for about 86% of first-half revenue.

deduped_items.title: Salvage mission begins as navy battles to raise capsized Java Sea ferry
deduped_items.summary: BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger f...
deduped_items.body_text:
BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger ferry that went down in the Java Sea last week, a navy official said, with dozens of people still missing.
The Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact with its shipping company after departing from Indonesia’s second city of Surabaya on Java island on Sunday, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo island.
At least six people have died and 129 are missing, according to the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas. Some of the victims are feared trapped inside the vessel, which is now submerged.
An expert team has been brought in to assist the operation to right the ferry, local navy commander Galih Nurna Putra told reporters on Friday.
“The salvage operation is underway,” Galih said, adding that “there was an observation yesterday”.
The head of the Banjarmasin search and rescue agency, I Putu Sudayana, said teams would be able to resume the recovery of bodies once the vessel is righted.
Before that process is completed, divers face risks if they try to enter the capsized ship, he said.
“We understand the psychological condition of the victims’ families, but please also understand the situation faced by the joint search and rescue team, because they must also pay attention to (operational) safety.”
The capsized vessel has drifted from its original position and sunk farther into the sea, from an initial depth of 21 metres (69 feet) to 29 metres, Basarnas operation director Yudhi Bramantyo said on Thursday.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Thursday, rescuers formally called off a search for eight people, including five journalists sent to cover a volcanic eruption, nearly two weeks after their speedboat went missing in waters between Java and Sumatra islands. — AFP
deduped_items.normalised_title: salvage mission begins as navy battles to raise capsized java sea ferry

deduped_items.title: Philippine Coast Guard seizes 12.5 tonnes ammonium nitrate, dynamite aboard Palawan ferry
deduped_items.summary: MANILA, Sept 18 — The Philippine Coast Guard said on Friday it confiscated 12.5 tonnes of ammonium nitrate and 130...
deduped_items.body_text:
MANILA, Sept 18 — The Philippine Coast Guard said on Friday it confiscated 12.5 tonnes of ammonium nitrate and 130 cases of dynamite aboard a vessel sitting at port in Palawan province.
The explosive substances were found on Sunday alongside materials used in detonations inside two trucks on a ferry that carried both cargo and passengers, the coast guard said in a statement.
Ammonium nitrate, a chemical used in fertilisers, is safe if stored properly, but there can be catastrophic consequences when mishandled or mixed with explosives.
A stash of 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate left to degrade in a Beirut warehouse killed more than 220 people and laid waste to swathes of the Lebanese capital when it exploded in 2020.
“The explosives and components were discovered inside (two trucks) aboard the RoRo (roll-on, roll-off) passenger vessel,” the coast guard said in a Friday statement, adding the cargo had been “improperly declared”.
“The confiscated explosives and components are currently under the custody of the Philippine National Police,” they said.
“The (coast guard) will work closely with the PNP to determine the role of the accompanying personnel in the shipment of said cargo.”
It was unclear if any arrests had been made as of Friday afternoon, and the name of the involved company has not been disclosed.
A coast guard officer tasked with port safety had been “relieved from his post to ensure impartial investigation”, the statement said.
The discovery comes in the wake of a series of deadly ferry accidents.
On September 9, a fire ripped after an explosion in the cargo hold of the M/V June Aster near the resort area of Coron, Palawan, burning dozens of passengers to death.
In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Witness says attack was ‘like a scene off Jaws’ as shark kills swimmer in Western Australia
deduped_items.summary: SYDNEY, Sept 18 — A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia today, polic...
deduped_items.body_text:
SYDNEY, Sept 18 — A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia today, police said.
It was the fourth death from a shark attack in Australia this year.
“It was reported a male swimmer had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast,” a Western Australia state police spokeswoman said in a statement.
“The swimmer died as a result of the attack.”
Police helicopters and boats scoured waters off Sorrento Beach after emergency services were called to the beach in the morning, officials said.
Authorities closed beaches in the area until further notice.
Local media reported that witnesses had seen blood in the water.
“It was like a scene off Jaws where a body is flicked around like a rag doll,” an unidentified male witness on the beach told local broadcaster Seven.
Surf Life Saving WA said in a social media post that an unidentified species of shark was involved in the incident about 50 metres offshore.
It was the second shark attack in Western Australia this week, after a man lost part of his leg when he was bitten at Glenfield Beach, north of Perth.
There have been multiple shark attack fatalities around the country this year.
A 12-year-old boy died after he was bitten by a shark while swimming in Sydney Harbour in January.
Three divers were fatally mauled in separate incidents between May and June — two in Western Australia and the third in Queensland.
Also in June, a woman had to have part of her left arm amputated after she was mauled by a shark at one of Australia’s most popular beaches, Coogee, in Sydney.
There have been around 1,300 shark incidents around Australia since 1791, of which more than 260 resulted in death, according to a database of their encounters with humans. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Salvage mission begins as navy battles to raise capsized Java Sea ferry
deduped_items.summary: BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger f...
deduped_items.body_text:
BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger ferry that went down in the Java Sea last week, a navy official said, with dozens of people still missing.
The Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact with its shipping company after departing from Indonesia’s second city of Surabaya on Java island on Sunday, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo island.
At least six people have died and 129 are missing, according to the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas. Some of the victims are feared trapped inside the vessel, which is now submerged.
An expert team has been brought in to assist the operation to right the ferry, local navy commander Galih Nurna Putra told reporters on Friday.
“The salvage operation is underway,” Galih said, adding that “there was an observation yesterday”.
The head of the Banjarmasin search and rescue agency, I Putu Sudayana, said teams would be able to resume the recovery of bodies once the vessel is righted.
Before that process is completed, divers face risks if they try to enter the capsized ship, he said.
“We understand the psychological condition of the victims’ families, but please also understand the situation faced by the joint search and rescue team, because they must also pay attention to (operational) safety.”
The capsized vessel has drifted from its original position and sunk farther into the sea, from an initial depth of 21 metres (69 feet) to 29 metres, Basarnas operation director Yudhi Bramantyo said on Thursday.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Thursday, rescuers formally called off a search for eight people, including five journalists sent to cover a volcanic eruption, nearly two weeks after their speedboat went missing in waters between Java and Sumatra islands. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Salvage mission begins as navy battles to raise capsized Java Sea ferry
deduped_items.summary: BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger f...
deduped_items.body_text:
BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger ferry that went down in the Java Sea last week, a navy official said, with dozens of people still missing.
The Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact with its shipping company after departing from Indonesia’s second city of Surabaya on Java island on Sunday, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo island.
At least six people have died and 129 are missing, according to the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas. Some of the victims are feared trapped inside the vessel, which is now submerged.
An expert team has been brought in to assist the operation to right the ferry, local navy commander Galih Nurna Putra told reporters on Friday.
“The salvage operation is underway,” Galih said, adding that “there was an observation yesterday”.
The head of the Banjarmasin search and rescue agency, I Putu Sudayana, said teams would be able to resume the recovery of bodies once the vessel is righted.
Before that process is completed, divers face risks if they try to enter the capsized ship, he said.
“We understand the psychological condition of the victims’ families, but please also understand the situation faced by the joint search and rescue team, because they must also pay attention to (operational) safety.”
The capsized vessel has drifted from its original position and sunk farther into the sea, from an initial depth of 21 metres (69 feet) to 29 metres, Basarnas operation director Yudhi Bramantyo said on Thursday.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Thursday, rescuers formally called off a search for eight people, including five journalists sent to cover a volcanic eruption, nearly two weeks after their speedboat went missing in waters between Java and Sumatra islands. — AFP

BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger ferry that went down in the Java Sea last week, a navy official said, with dozens of people still missing.
The Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact with its shipping company after departing from Indonesia’s second city of Surabaya on Java island on Sunday, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo island.
At least six people have died and 129 are missing, according to the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas. Some of the victims are feared trapped inside the vessel, which is now submerged.
An expert team has been brought in to assist the operation to right the ferry, local navy commander Galih Nurna Putra told reporters on Friday.
“The salvage operation is underway,” Galih said, adding that “there was an observation yesterday”.
The head of the Banjarmasin search and rescue agency, I Putu Sudayana, said teams would be able to resume the recovery of bodies once the vessel is righted.
Before that process is completed, divers face risks if they try to enter the capsized ship, he said.
“We understand the psychological condition of the victims’ families, but please also understand the situation faced by the joint search and rescue team, because they must also pay attention to (operational) safety.”
The capsized vessel has drifted from its original position and sunk farther into the sea, from an initial depth of 21 metres (69 feet) to 29 metres, Basarnas operation director Yudhi Bramantyo said on Thursday.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Thursday, rescuers formally called off a search for eight people, including five journalists sent to cover a volcanic eruption, nearly two weeks after their speedboat went missing in waters between Java and Sumatra islands. — AFP

deduped_items.body_text:
PESHAWAR: Five cops were among 16 martyred in an explosion at Kohat Police Lines, according to officials.
Footage aired on television showed citizens gathered next to a building with a collapsed wall, digging through rubble and helping the injured.
The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.
Speaking to Dawn, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed confirmed the death toll, adding that more than 50 people were injured.
He told Dawn that a vehicle-borne suicide bomber initially struck the building’s gate. He said that some headed towards the Counter Terrorism Department building, where they were neutralised, while around three went to the Special Branch building.
An initial handout from IG Hameed said the explosion occurred at a mosque at Kohat Police Lines. It added that initial reports suggested an explosive-laden vehicle was rammed into the building.
In a later statement, he said that a suicide bomber detonated himself near the Special Branch building, adding that an exchange of fire was underway with Fitna al Khawarij terrorists.
“The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high.
Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.
At around 3:30pm, police said the clearance operation was “in its final stages”.
The statement detailed that seven terrorists had attempted to infiltrate Police Lines after the explosion.
“So far, six terrorists, including a suicide bomber, have been killed,” the statement said.
Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office.
He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying.
In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines.
Condemnations pour in
President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.
President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported.
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured.
“The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”.
A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved.
“The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying.
This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

deduped_items.body_text:
PESHAWAR: Five cops were among 16 martyred in an explosion at Kohat Police Lines, according to officials.
Footage aired on television showed citizens gathered next to a building with a collapsed wall, digging through rubble and helping the injured.
The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.
Speaking to Dawn, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed confirmed the death toll, adding that more than 50 people were injured.
He told Dawn that a vehicle-borne suicide bomber initially struck the building’s gate. He said that some headed towards the Counter Terrorism Department building, where they were neutralised, while around three went to the Special Branch building.
An initial handout from IG Hameed said the explosion occurred at a mosque at Kohat Police Lines. It added that initial reports suggested an explosive-laden vehicle was rammed into the building.
In a later statement, he said that a suicide bomber detonated himself near the Special Branch building, adding that an exchange of fire was underway with Fitna al Khawarij terrorists.
“The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high.
Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.
At around 3:30pm, police said the clearance operation was “in its final stages”.
The statement detailed that seven terrorists had attempted to infiltrate Police Lines after the explosion.
“So far, six terrorists, including a suicide bomber, have been killed,” the statement said.
Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office.
He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying.
In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines.
Condemnations pour in
President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.
President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported.
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured.
“The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”.
A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved.
“The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying.
This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

deduped_items.title: CGA plans a historic 2027 visit to Philippines
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            CGA plans a historic 2027 visit to PhilippinesGEOPOLITICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The CGA’s nonmilitary role makes it a tool to avert diplomatic issues, an official said, while confirming the donation of a ship to Manila
  - By Lo Tien-pin and Jake Chung / Staff reporter, with staff writer and CNA
 Coast Guard Administration (CGA) ships are scheduled to sail to the Philippines bearing the words “Taiwan Coast Guard” in a high-profile visit in October next year, the first such visit by a Taiwanese maritime law enforcement vessel to the Southeast Asian nation, the agency said yesterday. The CGA also confirmed that it had donated one of its decommissioned patrol vessels to the Philippines in a rare transfer of a retired ship to a nondiplomatic ally. The Republic of China (ROC) Navy last made such a visit in 1974, shortly before the Philippines switched diplomatic recognition to the People’s Republic of China in 1975. The Lienchiang Coast Guard Administration vessel sails in an undated photograph.Photo courtesy of the Coast Guard Administration Official naval visits between Taiwan and the Philippines have effectively halted for half a century, a senior government official said on condition of anonymity. Unlike the navy’s goodwill missions, which involve an annual deployment of three ships intended to project force and conduct more sensitive operations, the CGA’s nonmilitary functions make it a more effective tool for overcoming Taiwan’s diplomatic difficulties, the official said. In September last year, the CGA’s 4,000-tonne Chiayi-class vessel Taipei (台北) visited Palau on a goodwill mission. The CGA’s planned visit to the Philippines next year would carry considerable geopolitical significance, the official said. Taiwan and the Philippines are both targets of China’s “gray zone” tactics, prompting the two sides to strengthen cooperation in maritime law enforcement and regional security, the official said. The efforts include the attendance of a senior Philippine Coast Guard official at Central Police University’s graduation ceremony last year and Taiwan’s donation of a retrofitted 500-tonne disaster relief and rescue vessel to the Philippines on Wednesday. According to media reports citing information from VesselFinder, a Philippine law enforcement vessel named Bling No. 1 sailed from the Port of Kaohsiung for sea trials before returning. Although stripped of its armaments and CGA markings, the vessel resembled the Lienchiang (連江), which was decommissioned on Oct. 27, 2023, or the Kinmen (金門). The CGA said in a statement that the transfer was “handled according to usual practice.” The Ministry of Foreign Affairs declined to comment on whether it was the first time Taiwan had donated a vessel to the Philippines. Su Tzu-yu (蘇紫雲), a research fellow at the Institute for National Defense and Security Research, said the donation was part of an international trend to counter China’s “expansionist behavior” at sea. Japan is to transfer decommissioned Abukuma-class destroyer escorts to the Philippines, while the US has transferred many patrol boats to the country, Su said. “China’s gray zone threats have prompted collaboration between the ‘white fleets,’” Su said. “This shows that Beijing’s actions have backfired.” Next year’s eight-day goodwill mission is to reportedly involve celestial navigation training using sextants, maritime operations and law enforcement instruction for 100 CGA personnel and students in Central Police University’s Department of Maritime Police. The trip is to facilitate exchanges with the Philippines on non-traditional security issues, including maritime humanitarian assistance and combating crime at sea. The approach would not only help reduce political sensitivities among neighboring countries, but also demonstrate Taiwan’s flexibility and adaptability as a maritime nation, the official said.

deduped_items.body_text:

            Central bank keeps key rates unchangedFED UP: The governor of Taiwan’s central bank said that there is still time to observe, while stock markets around the world mostly rose after the US Fed hiked interest rates
  - By Crystal Hsu / Staff reporter
 The central bank yesterday kept its key interest rates unchanged for a 10th straight quarter while easing housing credit controls, signaling confidence that property lending has cooled enough to allow a targeted relaxation without undermining financial stability. The central bank left its discount rate at 2 percent, the collateralized lending rate at 2.375 and the short-term lending rate at 4.25 percent. However, it increased the maximum loan-to-value ratio for people buying a second home to 70 percent from 60 percent and ended a restriction on loans for land purchases. Central bank Governor Yang Chin-long speaks at a news conference at the bank in Taipei yesterday.Photo: CNA Central bank Governor Yang Chin-long (楊金龍) said that monetary policy has remained relatively tight since 2024, helping stabilize domestic prices and anchor inflation expectations. “We still have time to observe,” Yang said, adding that two central bank board members dissented, while the majority backed maintaining the current policy stance. Some members nevertheless warned that inflation still requires close monitoring, he said. The cautious approach reflects uncertainty over the global economic outlook and the potential effect of conflict in the Middle East on Taiwan’s prices and economy, Yang said. Domestic inflation is manageable this year and is expected to fall below 2 percent next year, while economic growth is expected to remain solid, he said. The central bank lifted its forecast for full-year economic growth to 11.48 percent and said it expects the pace to slow to 5.82 percent next year. It also raised its growth forecasts for this year’s consumer price index (CPI) and core CPI to 2.03 percent and 2.16 percent respectively, putting both above its 2 percent inflation watch level. The easing in housing comes as property lending has continued to moderate. Real-estate loans accounted for 34.44 percent of total bank lending at the end of July, down from 35.56 percent in March and 37.61 percent in June 2024. Credit flows into property have dropped, while first-home buyers account for a growing share of residential mortgage borrowers, Yang said. Lending for urban renewal and reconstruction of aging or unsafe buildings has also taken up a larger share of construction loans, he said. Housing transactions have cooled, with speculative activity declining and expectations of further home-price gains moderating, Yang said. The central bank also removed a requirement introduced in December 2021 that land loans be accompanied by a commitment to begin construction within a specified period. Yang cited labor shortages and difficulties disposing of excavated soil as factors that can delay projects. Commercial banks have gained more experience managing property-related credit risks after several years of tighter controls, giving the central bank room for a targeted relaxation of land-financing restrictions, Yang said. The bank also expects growth in broad money supply to exceed its 2.5-to-6.5 percent reference range this year and raised the upper end to 6.75 percent, citing robust artificial intelligence-related exports and investment, buoyant stock-market activity and a low comparison base. Global stock markets mostly rose yesterday after the US Federal Reserve delivered a widely expected interest rate hike, while falling oil prices and easing bond yields also helped calm inflation fears. The Fed on Wednesday lifted borrowing costs for the first time since 2023, despite US President Donald Trump’s demand for cuts, as Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh insisted on the need to combat inflation that has been “too high” for “too long.” Stock markets in Taipei, Tokyo, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington, Mumbai, Bangkok and

deduped_items.title: Takaichi retains key ministers in reshuffle
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Takaichi retains key ministers in reshuffle
  - AFP, TOKYO
 Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi yesterday retained her key ministers in a Cabinet reshuffle and made two appointments of Taiwan-friendly politicians. Takaichi — who has high approval ratings nearly a year into office — kept core members of her team, according to a Cabinet list announced by government spokesman Minoru Kihara. They include Kihara, Minister of Finance Satsuki Katayama, Minister of Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi and Minister of Defense Shinjiro Koizumi. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi speaks at a news conference at her office in Tokyo yesterday.Photo: AP The prime minister also made new appointments, with Hisayuki Fujii named minister for internal affairs and communications, and Takashi Yamashita returning as minister of justice. Fujii and Yamashita have represented the ruling Liberal Democratic Party in the “two-plus-two” policy dialogues with Taiwan. At the talks between the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the LDP, the two have engaged in face-to-face discussions on issues such as Taiwan Strait security. Fujii participated in the dialogue in 2024, while Yamashita engaged in the seventh, expanded edition of the dialogue on Monday with DPP representatives, including Legislator Puma Shen (沈伯洋), the party’s candidate for Taipei mayor. During the meeting, the LDP’s Taiwan policy project team identified enhancing deterrence, civil defense, “gray zone” contingencies and economic cooperation as areas for further discussion. While Fujii has engaged in Taiwan-Japan exchanges through the lens of diplomatic and security policies, Yamashita has been more involved in the internal deliberation of Taiwan policy within the LDP. The small-scale reshuffle comes as Takaichi navigates rising inflation and a weak yen while pursuing a consumption tax cut on food starting next year. While Takaichi’s tax cut pledge is popular among voters, economists have criticized the plan, warning that she has failed to identify about ￥5 trillion (US$32 billion) needed annually to fund it. Takaichi’s policy of expansive government spending has also rattled markets, pushing Japan’s benchmark bond yield to about 3 percent, its highest in three decades. With Katayama in the finance role, Japan has repeatedly intervened in the foreign exchange market to prop up the falling yen. On defense, Koizumi remains tasked with updating Japan’s foundational national defense strategy. “Revising our strategy is something that has a major impact on Japan’s security and on the entire region,” Koizumi told reporters after he was reappointed. The defense ministry “must marshal all our resources and move forward with a greater speed” with the review with “a strong sense of urgency,” he added. Additional reporting by Lin Tsuei-yi

The new policy was revealed after a screenshot of an email from the information engineering department at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) was posted to social media platform Threads on Friday. “Starting from the next class, attendance will.
deduped_items.body_text:
CUHK department triggers backlash over WeChat attendance registration policy
Screenshotted email has information engineering department telling students: ‘Please install the WeChat app and enable location services’
A department at Hong Kong’s second-oldest university has faced a backlash over asking students to use mainland Chinese messaging app WeChat to register their attendance and keep its location services enabled, later saying the decision was optional.
The new policy was revealed after a screenshot of an email from the information engineering department at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) was posted to social media platform Threads on Friday.
“Starting from the next class, attendance will be recorded by scanning a QR code through WeChat. Please install the WeChat app and enable location services before coming to class.”

China may be aiming to equip its sixth-generation fighter jets with laser weapons that experts say could help defend them against incoming missiles.

Screenshotted email has information engineering department telling students: ‘Please install the WeChat app and enable location services’
A department at Hong Kong’s second-oldest university has faced a backlash over asking students to use mainland Chinese messaging app WeChat to register their attendance and keep its location services enabled, later saying the decision was optional.
The new policy was revealed after a screenshot of an email from the information engineering department at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) was posted to social media platform Threads on Friday.
“Starting from the next class, attendance will be recorded by scanning a QR code through WeChat. Please install the WeChat app and enable location services before coming to class.”

deduped_items.summary: Hong Kong’s redeveloped Huanggang Port could begin operations as early as October 12, allowing cross-border travellers to complete dual immigration procedures in a single inspection under a new joint clearance system. deduped_items.title: New ‘world’s best airline’ crowned as Qantas fails to crack top 10
deduped_items.summary: Qatar Airways has lost the title of world’s best airline at the 2026 World Airline Awards, in a year when the highly regarded Middle East carrier has been disrupted by conflict in its region.
deduped_items.body_text:
New ‘world’s best airline’ crowned as Qantas fails to crack top 10
Qatar Airways has lost the title of world’s best airline at the 2026 World Airline Awards, in a year when the highly regarded Middle East carrier has been disrupted by conflict in its region.
Qatar was pipped by Singapore Airlines for the Airline of the Year, which took out the No.1 spot after the Gulf carrier won the previous two years.
Qatar Airways took second place – the position held by Singapore Airlines last year. It’s the sixth time Singapore Airlines has taken out the top award, a feat surpassed only by Qatar, which has won nine times.
Qantas, meanwhile, climbed two places from 14th to 12th this year, still far below its historical results where it consistently ranked in the top five, including as recently as 2022. However, the airline has continued to climb back from its nadir in 2024, where it fell to 24th amid a series of scandals including illegally sacking staff, selling fares for flights that had already been cancelled and criticisms over the availability of rewards seats for Frequent Flyer members.
Among Australia’s other airlines, Virgin Australian dropped three places to 37th, while Jetstar stayed in 88th place.
Sign up for the Traveller newsletter
The latest travel news, tips and inspiration delivered to your inbox. Sign up now.
As usual, Asian and Middle Eastern airlines dominated the top 10, with Hong Kong’s Cathay Pacific in third and Japan’s All Nippon Airways (ANA) in fourth. Rounding the top five was Turkish Airlines, which started flights between Australia and Istanbul via Asia in 2024 and plans non-stop flights between Australia and Turkey next year.
Singapore Airlines also won the award for world’s best economy class and best economy class catering, and was runner-up business class (behind Qatar Airways) and first class (behind Air France).
The airline reported record revenue of $6.28 billion for the first quarter of this financial year, even as it slumped to an $83 million net loss due to conflict in the Middle East causing fuel prices to surge.
This year a new award, for best onboard Wi-Fi, went to Qatar Airways. It was the only category in which US airlines dominated, taking all other slots in the top five behind Qatar (Delta Air Lines, United, Alaska Airlines and JetBlue).
The World Airline Awards are based on online customer-satisfaction surveys conducted by consultancy firm Skytrax, with passengers from 100 countries taking part and more than 350 airlines featuring in the final results. Skytrax claims the awards are based on the world’s largest airline satisfaction survey.
Some aviation experts have questioned Skytrax’s methodology and the lack of transparency in its awards process. According to some reports, Skytrax has refused to answer questions related to how its survey system works or even what the business actually does.
Airlines, however, are quick to trumpet the results when favourable.

Qatar Airways has lost the title of world’s best airline at the 2026 World Airline Awards, in a year when the highly regarded Middle East carrier has been disrupted by conflict in its region.
Qatar was pipped by Singapore Airlines for the Airline of the Year, which took out the No.1 spot after the Gulf carrier won the previous two years.
Qatar Airways took second place – the position held by Singapore Airlines last year. It’s the sixth time Singapore Airlines has taken out the top award, a feat surpassed only by Qatar, which has won nine times.
Qantas, meanwhile, climbed two places from 14th to 12th this year, still far below its historical results where it consistently ranked in the top five, including as recently as 2022. However, the airline has continued to climb back from its nadir in 2024, where it fell to 24th amid a series of scandals including illegally sacking staff, selling fares for flights that had already been cancelled and criticisms over the availability of rewards seats for Frequent Flyer members.
Among Australia’s other airlines, Virgin Australian dropped three places to 37th, while Jetstar stayed in 88th place.
